name: Magnetometer
plain: Reads the magnetic field around the device, like a compass.
meaning: Gives compass heading and can reveal nearby metal and electronics. Indoor magnetic fields form a rough fingerprint of a building or room.

access.prompt_ui: Chromium shows no bubble: access follows the Motion sensors site setting (default Allow) plus the Permissions API name. Safari and Firefox do not ship the API.
access.persistence: Site setting Allow or Block per origin
access.iframe: Cross-origin iframes blocked unless allow="magnetometer"; page must be focused and visible
steps: 'reading' events fire; 'error' event on NotAllowedError or NotReadableError

samsung.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

data.metric: Sensor readings at the requested frequency

fields.name: x, y, z
fields.range: about -4900 to 4900 hardware; Earth field 25 to 65

limits.headline: Can sense the magnetic field around your device, like a compass
limits.user_action: Nothing in most browsers. Chrome allows it by default unless you changed Motion sensors in site settings
can: Find which way your device points, like a compass
Guess which room or building you are in from its magnetic pattern, roughly
cannot: Run in Firefox or Safari, which do not support it
Show a prompt in Chrome; there is none by default
Measure the field while the page is closed
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet support it. Safari and Firefox do not.

story.what_it_is: The page reads the magnetic field around your device, like a compass.

marketing.name: Generic Sensor API
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes a common way for web pages to read motion and environment sensors such as accelerometer and gyroscope.

story.for_you: A compass or a map turns to match where you face. You may not see a prompt. Nearby metal and electronics change what the sensor reads.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for compass features and AR. Indoor magnetic patterns can help place a person in a building, and they are also a rough fingerprint of where a device has been.

use_cases.example: A web map or hiking page turns to the direction you face.
A web AR scene lines up virtual objects with north.
A treasure hunt or location web game points you toward the next clue.
A museum or airport web app uses magnetic maps to guide people indoors.
A fraud tool may check whether a phone reads believable magnetic data, since an emulator does not.
A tracker uses the readings to build a rough fingerprint of the device and its surroundings.

history.change: Magnetometer ships with the Generic Sensor API
